runs.t: Replication maintains multiple copies of data for availability, read scale or geographic proximity. Strategies differ in who accepts writes and how replicas become consistent.
Understand leader-follower, multi-leader and leaderless models, synchronous versus asynchronous acknowledgment, lag, failover and split-brain prevention. State read-after-write guarantees explicitly.
A news site serves most reads from replicas, while editorial publishing routes writes through a leader. After publishing, an editor may require routing to the primary until the update is visible.
Replicas are not backups: corruption or accidental deletion can replicate too. Automatic failover may lose unacknowledged writes depending on guarantees; monitor lag and restore behavior.
